seo_title: Cost of Living in Phuket 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Phuket per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: A tropical island with a large Russian-speaking community of freelancers and visa-free entry for 60 days. The ocean, a warm climate year-round and a developed infrastructure for remote work.
pros: Visa-free entry for 60 days with an option to extend
The ocean and a warm climate year-round
A large Russian-speaking community, especially in Rawai and Chalong
A developed infrastructure for remote work
cons: Rainy season from May to October — frequent downpours and rough seas
High rental costs during the tourist season
Transport is limited without a car or scooter
Difficulties with international payments from Russia

best_places.name: Rawai
best_places.description: The quiet south of the island, with a seafood market and a large Russian community — a favourite of families.

best_places.name: Patong
best_places.description: The island's tourist hub: nightlife, cafés, shopping and Patong Beach.

best_places.name: Hatch Coworking
best_places.description: Chalong's main coworking for nomads — open 24/7, with events and open-space areas.

best_places.name: Old Phuket Town
best_places.description: Sino-Portuguese mansions, street art and coffee shops — the historic heart of the island.

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 60 days without a visa on a passport, extendable by 30 days at immigration.

visa_steps.title: Education Visa or DTV
visa_steps.description: A study visa or the Destination Thailand Visa (for nomads) — up to 5 years of stay.

visa_steps.title: Tax ID (TIN)
visa_steps.description: Needed for a bank account and a long-term stay — issued by the Revenue Department.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Kasikorn, Bangkok Bank — they open accounts with a visa and ID; it's harder for tourists.

visa_steps.title: Renting housing
visa_steps.description: Contracts from 6 months — pricier in the tourist season, with discounts up to 40% in the low season.

faq.question: When is the best season in Phuket?
faq.answer: November–April — dry, +28–32°C. May–October is the rainy season and cheaper.

faq.question: What are banks like in Phuket?
faq.answer: It's harder for Russians, but Kasikorn and Bangkok Bank open accounts with a visa and proof of residence.

faq.question: Can I move to Phuket with kids?
faq.answer: Yes, there are many international schools (UWC Thailand, BCIS, HeadStart) and private kindergartens.

faq.question: What's the internet like in Phuket?
faq.answer: Fibre at 300+ Mbps for 1,500–2,000 ₽, with 4G/5G everywhere. Suitable for remote work.

faq.question: How do I get to Russia?
faq.answer: There are no direct flights; convenient connections run via Dubai, Doha and Istanbul — 14–18 hours.

faq.question: Which district should I choose in Phuket?
faq.answer: Families — Rawai and Chalong. Nightlife — Patong and Kamala. Quiet life — Nai Harn and Nai Yang.

reviews.text: I moved my family to Rawai: a house with a pool for 80,000 ₽, my daughter at UWC. The main thing — the ocean is 10 minutes away and the healthcare is reasonable.
I've wintered in Phuket three years running: coworking, surfing, friends. In summer I head back to Moscow — you get tired of the humidity.
